newsitem.title: USA: PS New Hampshire sees 320 MW unit up today.
newsitem.headline: PS New Hampshire sees 320 MW unit up today.

text.p: Public Service of New Hampshire expected 320 megawatt (MW) coal-fired unit 2 at its Merrimack power plant to resume service today after being shut Thursday due to a boiler tube leak, the company said Friday.
"It's being started now," said company spokesman Martin Murray, adding the leak resulted in an explosive noise over the plant.
"There was a very loud sound when the steam vented to the atmosphere," he said.
Meanwhile, an adjoining 113 MW coal unit will be shut for scheduled maintenance later today, Murray said.
Merrimack's unit 1 will be out of service six to eight weeks, he said.
The Merrimack facility, located near the town of Bow in central New Hampshire, accounts for roughly one-quarter of the utility's instate generation capacity.
Public Service of New Hampshire is a subsidiary of Northeast Utilities.
